coverage_notes: Third closure of Batch 5's disclosed broader-scope gap (SS14 Requalification Trigger). Complements the pre-existing onsure-release-qualification.v1.schema.json / assurance.release.qualify (Batch 5 slice 4, which qualifies a release as of one point in time) by deciding whether that qualification must be redone at all, and with what scope. SS14 names 9 independent trigger conditions but does not itself define a full-vs-partial rule -- this closure commits to one, explicitly disclosed: sandbox/TCB/crypto change, a confirmed MissedFinding blind spot, or a weakened severity/coverage policy are trust-boundary-level changes that force FULL requalification regardless of any other flag (a narrower, localized change alone can never widen scope past what a trust-boundary change already requires); the remaining 6 triggers force only PARTIAL when no FULL-tier trigger is also present. requalificationTriggerEvaluateFullTierWinsButListsEveryTriggeredReasonNotJustTheFullOne proves triggered_reasons lists every true flag (oracle_rubric_changed, adapter_plugin_changed, sandbox_tcb_crypto_changed, in ALL_REQUALIFICATION_TRIGGERS iteration order) even though only the FULL-tier one decided the scope -- matching this session's established 'aggregate, do not short-circuit' precedent, now applied a third time in this same broader-scope pass (after FR-META-041 and the AI Currentness closure).
open_gap: Operates on caller-supplied trigger flags; there is no live change-detection system in this codebase that observes validator/oracle/adapter/benchmark/sandbox/dependency/policy changes and sets these flags automatically (same disclosed 'caller-supplied representation, not live system read' pattern as every other Batch 5 broader-scope closure this session). The full-vs-partial severity split (which 3 of the 9 triggers are trust-boundary-level) is an inferred, disclosed convention, not literally specified by SS14.
